purpose: Canonical teaching ontology and source-to-topic gap matrix for the ten supplied PDFs.

statusDefinitions.adequate: Current material teaches the concept with distinct explanation and practice.
statusDefinitions.shallow: Named or grouped, but lacks concept-specific mechanism, example, procedure, or evidence.
statusDefinitions.source_only: Source-specific or time-sensitive claim that must be taught as attributed evidence, not universal fact.

sequencing.goal: Understand agent behavior, goals, loops, evidence, and human control.
Prompt, explore repositories, manage sessions, use the terminal, and verify changes.
Encode instructions, test, review, isolate, and coordinate work safely.
Design tools, hooks, subagents, non-interactive jobs, and bounded autonomous loops.
Evaluate, observe, recover, scale teams, and maintain knowledge systems.

topics.title: Persistent goals versus finite tasks
topics.nuance: A goal persists across observations; a task has an endpoint. Teach explicit stop conditions with goals.

topics.title: Observe–decide–act–check loop
topics.nuance: Separate loop stages and show how external evidence changes the next action.

topics.title: Reflection as a measurable correction rule
topics.nuance: Reflection is not open-ended self-critique; it compares output with a named criterion.

topics.title: Explicit stopping conditions
topics.nuance: Distinguish completion, budget, time, error, risk, and escalation stops.

topics.title: Harness engineering
topics.nuance: The harness is the environment of tools, context, permissions, feedback, and state—not the model alone.

topics.title: Loop engineering
topics.nuance: General loop design must remain separate from the source-specific Ralph implementation.

topics.title: Executable prompt briefs
topics.nuance: Teach outcome, evidence, constraints, non-goals, ambiguity policy, and verification as distinct fields.

topics.title: AskUserQuestion and material ambiguity
topics.nuance: Ask questions only when answers alter scope, architecture, risk, or acceptance criteria.

topics.title: Voice input for high-bandwidth context
topics.nuance: Messy dictation can preserve constraints, contradictions, and failed attempts; require clarification and a written brief afterward.

topics.title: Screenshots as design evidence
topics.nuance: Use a visual reference to communicate layout, then specify what to copy and what not to copy.

topics.title: Edit or branch before a bad trajectory
topics.nuance: Ruben recommends editing the earlier prompt; YK describes fork/half-clone. Present both as trajectory repair patterns.

topics.title: Share dislikes and negative examples
topics.nuance: A concrete rejected example can constrain taste better than vague positive adjectives.

topics.title: Choose the right abstraction level
topics.nuance: Too low-level micromanages; too high-level removes invariants and verification.

topics.title: Plan deliberately and prototype quickly
topics.nuance: Use spikes for unknowns and plans for dependencies; do not turn either into dogma.

topics.title: Map an unfamiliar repository
topics.nuance: Require file-backed claims about entry points, flows, tests, and conventions.

topics.title: Dependency-aware task decomposition
topics.nuance: Split on independently verifiable outcomes and real dependencies, not arbitrary file counts.

topics.title: Large-codebase index files
topics.nuance: Generate navigational indexes, cite them from CLAUDE.md, and keep them refreshable.

topics.title: Simplify overcomplicated generated code
topics.nuance: After correctness, ask for a simplification pass constrained by tests and public behavior.

topics.title: Context engineering
topics.nuance: Select, structure, refresh, and remove context; more context is not automatically better.

topics.title: Fresh sessions and context decay
topics.nuance: Treat Ruben's turn counts as anecdotal, not product guarantees; teach symptom-based reset decisions.

topics.title: Proactive compaction and handoff documents
topics.nuance: A handoff preserves goal, completed work, decisions, remaining tasks, verification, and hazards.

topics.title: Search conversation history
topics.nuance: Teach safe local search and extracting user messages without leaking session data.

topics.title: Memory architecture and retention policy
topics.nuance: Separate working context, durable instructions, episodic progress, and external knowledge.

topics.title: Explicit task state management
topics.nuance: Represent queued, active, blocked, verified, failed, and done states explicitly.

topics.title: Connector selection and context cost
topics.nuance: Ruben's token-cost claim is source-specific and time-sensitive; teach least-context connector selection and purposeful combinations.

topics.title: Projects for fixed material versus creative work
topics.nuance: Preserve as Ruben's workflow opinion: fixed recurring corpus benefits from Projects; blank context may help novelty.

topics.title: CLAUDE.md as memory, boundary, and primer
topics.nuance: Teach what belongs, what does not, and how instructions become stale.

topics.title: CLAUDE.md hierarchy, scopes, and monorepos
topics.nuance: Show load scopes and place rules at the narrowest stable level.

topics.title: Progressive disclosure and modular instructions
topics.nuance: Keep the root concise; link conditional detail and indexes instead of preloading everything.

topics.title: Executable workflow definitions in CLAUDE.md
topics.nuance: Encode ordered procedures plus checks for recurring repository operations.

topics.title: Conditional and path-specific instructions
topics.nuance: Load special rules only when the file, task, or tool condition applies.

topics.title: CLAUDE.md maintenance and version control
topics.nuance: Update with PRs, capture discoveries, review periodically, and version changes.

topics.title: CLAUDE.md versus skills, commands, hooks, plugins, and MCP
topics.nuance: Decision must be based on automatic context, invocation, determinism, reuse, and external access.

topics.title: Skills as reusable capabilities
topics.nuance: Sources disagree in scope: Hamza/YK emphasize reuse; Ruben advises fixed repeated tasks rather than creative work.

topics.title: Hooks for deterministic enforcement
topics.nuance: Use hooks for machine-enforceable checks, not vague judgment; explain failure and bypass paths.

topics.title: MCP selection and documentation
topics.nuance: Document server purpose, capabilities, authentication, allowed operations, and fallback.

topics.title: Slash commands, status line, aliases, and input controls
topics.nuance: These are distinct ergonomics: visibility, command recall, shell launch, and prompt editing.

topics.title: dx plugin, quick setup, and multiple accounts
topics.nuance: Later YK tips appear in the index but extracted PDF detail is limited; flag exact coverage limitation.

topics.title: Tool design and clear interfaces
topics.nuance: Teach narrow schemas, descriptive errors, idempotency, observability, and safe defaults.

topics.title: Capture terminal output as agent evidence
topics.nuance: Use tmux or logs to send, capture, inspect, and bound long-running commands.

topics.title: Use absolute paths with realpath
topics.nuance: Absolute paths reduce ambiguity across processes, containers, and automation.

topics.title: Browser research and blocked-site fallback
topics.nuance: Separate source retrieval, browser interaction, alternate legitimate access, evidence capture, and citation.

topics.title: Artifacts and persistent mini-apps
topics.nuance: Distinguish static visualization, interactive data, persisted state, and embedding Claude.

topics.title: HTML as an editable visual artifact
topics.nuance: Teach as Ruben's practical workaround; do not generalize the claim that Claude cannot generate images across products or time.

topics.title: Claude Code as a universal computer interface
topics.nuance: Power comes from composable shell/files/API access; risk grows with ambient authority.

topics.title: Verification targets and evidence hierarchy
topics.nuance: Match verification to claim: tests, types, lint, runtime, UI screenshot, diff, logs, or human judgment.

topics.title: Closed write–test–inspect cycle
topics.nuance: A command running is not evidence; capture its result and compare it with expectation.

topics.title: Test-driven development with an agent
topics.nuance: Write and observe failing tests, commit intent, then implement; guard against tests that merely mirror implementation.

topics.title: Diff review and independent reviewer sessions
topics.nuance: Separate author and reviewer context; review behavior, scope, tests, security, and hidden assumptions.

topics.title: Agent evaluation design
topics.nuance: Use representative tasks, measurable graders, regression sets, and failure taxonomy—not demo anecdotes.

topics.title: Observability and tracing
topics.nuance: Record tool calls, state transitions, decisions, latency, cost, errors, and artifacts while protecting secrets.

topics.title: Git and GitHub CLI as control surfaces
topics.nuance: Git supplies checkpoints, diffs, blame, branch isolation, and reviewable history—not just backup.

topics.title: Git worktrees for parallel branches
topics.nuance: Assign branch, directory, files, and integration owner; worktrees do not prevent semantic collisions.

topics.title: Interactive pull-request review
topics.nuance: Fetch review context, inspect each comment against code, implement selectively, rerun checks, and summarize dispositions.

topics.title: DevOps and CI investigation
topics.nuance: Read pipeline config and logs, reproduce narrowly, preserve deployment boundaries, and avoid blind retries.

topics.title: Guardrails as enforceable boundaries
topics.nuance: Separate policy statements from technical enforcement and test both allow and deny paths.

topics.title: Permissions and human approval gates
topics.nuance: Place gates at irreversible, external, costly, ambiguous, or security-sensitive transitions.

topics.title: Risk-tiered autonomy
topics.nuance: Match permission mode and isolation to blast radius; never teach blanket bypass as a default.

topics.title: Containers and isolated environments
topics.nuance: Isolation reduces host risk but does not remove credential, network, data, or supply-chain risk.

topics.title: Auto mode with bounded scope
topics.nuance: Teach prerequisites, approved commands, scope, monitoring, and abort conditions; product behavior may change.

topics.title: Orchestration patterns
topics.nuance: Compare sequential, parallel, router, supervisor, reviewer, and escalation patterns.

topics.title: Role-specialized multi-agent systems
topics.nuance: Ruben describes Cowork parallelism; general teaching must cover distinct outputs, handoffs, reviewer independence, and merge cost.

topics.title: Collision-free parallel work boundaries
topics.nuance: Define ownership, shared contracts, branch/worktree, completion artifact, and integrator.

topics.title: Background commands and subagents
topics.nuance: Background work needs identifiers, bounded polling, captured output, cancellation, and final verification.

topics.title: When Ralph loops fit—and when they do not
topics.nuance: Use for bounded, testable, file-observable iteration; avoid ambiguous taste, unsafe external effects, and weak verification.

topics.title: Ralph stop-hook core mechanism
topics.nuance: A completion promise is a control token, not proof; the hook recycles work until bounded conditions are met.

topics.title: PRD and atomic prd.json tasks
topics.nuance: Each task needs acceptance criteria, dependencies, priority, and machine-checkable completion.

topics.title: progress.txt and agents.md iteration memory
topics.nuance: Separate chronological execution log from durable project patterns and gotchas.

topics.title: Ralph feedback-loop architecture
topics.nuance: Tests, lint, builds, task state, git history, and memory become feedback channels.

topics.title: Manual, attended, and unattended Ralph levels
topics.nuance: Progress autonomy only after success at lower levels; add iteration, cost, time, and error budgets.

topics.title: Ralph feature, test, review, and POC patterns
topics.nuance: Teach four patterns separately; multi-persona review is not equivalent to independent external evaluation.

topics.title: Non-interactive and structured-output automation
topics.nuance: Cover one-off queries, structured output, streaming, exit codes, idempotency, and secret handling.

topics.title: Bounded polling and manual exponential backoff
topics.nuance: Polling needs maximum attempts, increasing intervals, success predicate, error exit, and final capture.

topics.title: Automation of automation
topics.nuance: Source index names the tip but extracted PDF lacks full body; retain as a coverage limitation and avoid invented detail.

topics.title: Remote and phone control
topics.nuance: Teach authentication, session visibility, network exposure, emergency stop, and audit trail.

topics.title: Graphify concept graph model
topics.nuance: A graph adds relationships and centrality; it does not guarantee truth or relevance.

topics.title: Obsidian export and reversible import
topics.nuance: Compare standalone vault, deletable folder, selected notes, and direct integration; stage before merging.

topics.title: Source backlinks and provenance
topics.nuance: Bare linked notes need source content and origin backlinks to support verification.

topics.title: Retrieval and review cadence for a second brain
topics.nuance: A commenter identifies an unresolved limitation: storage without a resurfacing routine becomes a graveyard.

topics.title: Claude Code for writing and Markdown
topics.nuance: Use files, diffs, version control, and structured Markdown for non-code work; Notion paste preservation is a narrow tactic.

topics.title: Invest in a personalized workflow
topics.nuance: Measure friction before adding tooling; maintain and remove customizations that no longer pay off.

topics.title: Deliberate practice, iterative problem solving, and sharing
topics.nuance: Practice on real work, keep evidence of failures and reusable discoveries, contribute improvements, and continue learning.

topics.title: Personalized software and mini-tools
topics.nuance: Lower implementation cost makes narrow personal tools viable; maintenance, privacy, and data portability still matter.

topics.title: Name, resume, and hand off sessions
topics.nuance: Session naming aids retrieval; resumption still requires checking goal, repository state, prior decisions, and remaining verification.

topics.title: Fan-out batch work
topics.nuance: Use a stable input set, one isolated invocation per item, structured results, concurrency bounds, retry policy, and aggregation.

topics.title: Organize CLAUDE.md as WHY, HOW, and WHAT
topics.nuance: Explain project purpose and architecture, operational commands, and repository map without turning the file into exhaustive documentation.

topics.title: Create and bootstrap CLAUDE.md safely
topics.nuance: Compare generated initialization, manual authoring, and incremental memory capture; review generated claims against the repository.

topics.title: Acquire and normalize an authoritative corpus
topics.nuance: Define canonical sources, retrieval boundaries, document identity, update date, and failed acquisitions before graph construction.

topics.title: Enrich bare graph nodes with useful content
topics.nuance: A title and backlinks are not a useful note; add source-grounded explanation, relationship meaning, and provenance without inventing content.

topics.title: Diagnose and recover from common agent failures
topics.nuance: Classify context overload, vague requests, unchecked output, runaway scope, repeated failed edits, and unsafe automation; choose rewind, clarify, isolate, re-plan, or restart accordingly.

topics.title: System-prompt slimming and patching
topics.nuance: This is risky anecdotal customization that can remove safety or product assumptions and become stale after upgrades; teach only with warnings and a reversible alternative.

topics.title: Model and effort routing
topics.nuance: Model names, pricing, and availability are time-sensitive. Preserve Ruben's principle—spend more reasoning on framing—without presenting current names as durable guidance.

topics.title: Code versus Cowork and Cowork parallelism
topics.nuance: Product comparison is Ruben's dated opinion; extract the durable distinction between coding tools and multi-agent knowledge-work coordination.

topics.title: Enterprise seat and privacy claims
topics.nuance: Pricing, thresholds, and privacy comparisons are high-change claims. Cite and date them; require current official verification before operational decisions.

topics.title: Creative-work and adoption opinions
topics.nuance: Includes writing-style, Research mode, loop-engineering, platform-switching, and commercial-success opinions. Teach as provocative heuristics, not facts.

evidenceRecordMappings.mappingRule: Every one of the 166 forensic concept records appears in topicEvidenceRecords or sourceOnlyEvidenceRecords. Repeated source records may support the same canonical topic; atomic evidence is not automatically a standalone curriculum topic.

r25-15.reason: Risky anecdotal system-prompt modification; retain with warning, not as standard practice.

rub-01.reason: Author workflow opinion about Projects and creativity.

rub-02.reason: Time-sensitive model names, effort modes, and pricing.

rub-03.reason: Product-capability framing is time-sensitive; preserve the HTML workflow.

rub-09.reason: Dated product comparison presented as author opinion.

rub-10.reason: Dated Cowork product behavior and author recommendation.

rub-15.reason: Commercial seat threshold and pricing can change.

rub-19.reason: Business-outcome opinion, not Claude Code technique.

rub-21.reason: Author skepticism about a product mode, not established fact.

rub-23.reason: Writing-style opinion; useful only as attributed heuristic.

rub-24.reason: Conflicts with engineering sources and is preserved as a simple-task counterposition.

rub-25.reason: Platform-loyalty advice is opinion rather than durable technique.

rub-26.reason: High-change security/privacy comparison requiring official current verification.

rub-27.reason: Anecdote about mathematical discovery, not an actionable Claude Code workflow.

positions: Official guidance emphasizes explore–plan–implement–commit for nontrivial changes.
YK recommends planning while prototyping quickly when uncertainty is the main risk.
conflictsAndNuances.resolution: Use a plan for known dependencies and a time-boxed spike for unknown feasibility; convert spike evidence into the implementation plan.

positions: Hamza/YK frame skills broadly as reusable capabilities.
Ruben argues skills fit repeated fixed tasks better than creative work.
conflictsAndNuances.resolution: Use skills for repeatable procedure, constraints, and tool access; keep creative judgment in the live brief.

positions: Several sources advise fresh, condensed context.
Projects and durable instructions help repeated work with stable source material.
conflictsAndNuances.resolution: Retain stable facts externally, but start execution sessions with a curated working set and clean trajectory.

positions: Ralph and YK show high-autonomy loops in isolated environments.
Official and agentic sources emphasize permissions, human gates, and verification.
conflictsAndNuances.resolution: Increase autonomy only as isolation, observability, reversibility, and machine-checkable acceptance increase.

positions: Agentic and Ralph sources treat loop design as a central engineering discipline.
Ruben dismisses trend-driven 'loop engineering' advice for ordinary users.
conflictsAndNuances.resolution: For routine interactive work, avoid ceremony. For repeated or unattended execution, explicit loops and stops are necessary engineering controls.
